75e878c762909dbc36e1e2100bdd0291.name: tdrive.file_upload
75e878c762909dbc36e1e2100bdd0291.description:
申请上传文件到网盘，返回临时上传 URL 和请求头。本工具不传文件内容，拿到返回后必须用 shell 执行 curl PUT 上传本地文件，再调 file_upload_complete 落库，否则网盘不会出现该文件。

上传命令（必须用 -T，让 curl 读取文件流式上传）：
curl -sSL -X PUT -H "K1: V1" -H "K2: V2" -T "/abs/path/to/file" "https://DOMAIN/PATH"

- URL = "https://" + 返回的 domain + path（path 已带 /，勿重复）
- 返回 headers 的每对 key/value 都用一个 -H 原样传入，勿省略改写
- -T 后必须是真实存在的本地文件路径

严禁 --data-binary "/path/to/file"，这会把路径字符串当 body 上传，curl 返回 0 看似成功但网盘里存的是一段路径文本。如需 --data-binary 必须加 @：--data-binary "@/path"。

curl exit code 0 且 stderr 空即成功，随后用返回的 confirm_key、task_id 调 file_upload_complete。下载用 file_download，建空目录用 dir_create。

75e878c762909dbc36e1e2100bdd0291.name: tdrive.file_download
75e878c762909dbc36e1e2100bdd0291.description: 为网盘已有文件签发临时下载 URL（约 60 分钟有效，请勿长期缓存；不能对目录使用）。⚠️ 重要：本工具只返回 download_url，不会返回文件内容。返回的 download_url 已包含 Token 签名，是一个完整可用的 URL，禁止对其做任何拆分、解析或修改，必须原样使用。获取到 URL 后，通过 shell 执行 curl 下载文件到本地，示例：curl -sSL -o OUTPUT_FILE "DOWNLOAD_URL" 将 DOWNLOAD_URL 替换为本工具返回的完整 download_url, OUTPUT_FILE 替换为本地保存路径（含文件名）。-S 显示错误、-s 静默进度、-L 自动跟随重定向（下载链接通常会 302 跳转）、-o 指定输出文件。用本工具：拿文件链接/下载地址。读正文/做内容总结优先 search_content；上传新文件用 file_upload。

75e878c762909dbc36e1e2100bdd0291.name: tdrive.dir_list
75e878c762909dbc36e1e2100bdd0291.description: 列出指定目录下的直接子项（文件 + 子目录），不递归。用本工具：已有 dir_id 想枚举其下内容。按文件名找用 search_file；按内容/语义找用 search_content。

75e878c762909dbc36e1e2100bdd0291.name: tdrive.dir_create
75e878c762909dbc36e1e2100bdd0291.description: 在指定父目录下创建一个空子目录（仅一层，不创建多级路径），返回新目录的 file_id。用本工具：明确想新建文件夹。上传文件用 file_upload；重命名已有目录用 file_rename；搬目录用 file_move。

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: GetMe
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: Bootstrap endpoint for agents. Retrieves authentication context including: available email aliases, permission scopes, rate limits (requests per minute/hour, daily send quota), and attachment constraints. Call this first to understand what operations are available.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: ListMessages
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: List email messages in a mailbox with pagination and flexible filtering. Supports filtering by: folder (inbox/sent/trash/spam), time range, attachment presence, and read status. Returns message summaries with sender, recipients, subject, snippet, and metadata. Use cursor-based pagination for large result sets.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: GetMessage
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: Retrieve full message content and metadata including: subject, sender, all recipients (to/cc/bcc), body (text or HTML), read status, attachment list (metadata only), threading headers (In-Reply-To, References), and original message reference for replies/forwards.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: SendMessage
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: Send a new email with support for multiple recipients, CC/BCC , and file attachments.IMPORTANT: This operation requires user confirmation. When you receive a CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED error, you MUST: 1) Display the operation_summary to the user showing what will be sent, 2) Explicitly ask the user to confirm, 3) Only retry with the confirmation_token after receiving user approval. NEVER auto-retry without user consent.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: ReplyMessage
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: Reply to an existing email. Automatically sets threading headers (In-Reply-To, References) to maintain conversation context. Supports: reply to sender only or reply-all (includes original recipients), additional CC/BCC, attachments, and plain/HTML formatting. IMPORTANT: Requires user confirmation - see SendMessage for confirmation workflow.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: ForwardMessage
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: Forward an existing email to new recipients. Preserves the original message content and optionally includes original attachments. You can add a comment/note at the beginning and attach additional files. IMPORTANT: Requires user confirmation - see SendMessage for confirmation workflow.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: DeleteMessage
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: Delete an email by moving it to trash. Messages remain in trash until permanently deleted. IMPORTANT: Requires user confirmation - see SendMessage for confirmation workflow.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: PermanentDeleteMessage
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: Permanently delete one email that is already in trash. The request is rejected if the message is not in trash. This operation is irreversible and does not require confirmation.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: ClearTrash
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: Permanently delete all messages in trash. This operation is irreversible and requires user confirmation: first call without confirmation_token, show the returned operation summary to the user, then retry with the token only after explicit approval.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: ListAttachments
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: List attachment metadata for a specific email without downloading the actual file content. Returns attachment IDs, filenames, MIME types, and file sizes.

f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.name: SearchMessages
f3934781f2c638baf55c36c5f961e3b4.description: Search emails with via the q parameter (matches subject and/or body), sender/recipient filtering, date range, folder, attachment presence, and read status. Returns matching messages with highlighted snippets showing where keywords were found. Use search_in to control search scope: SEARCH_IN_ALL (default, searches subject+body), SEARCH_IN_SUBJECT (subject only), SEARCH_IN_CONTENT (body only). Supports cursor-based pagination for large result sets.

a9346d6867266d5f76eb21ad50e8baa8.name: miora_write_canvas
a9346d6867266d5f76eb21ad50e8baa8.description:
Create or update a `.miora` canvas — a visual board that arranges images and videos, previewable inside WorkBuddy. Use it when the user wants a moodboard, a visual summary, a storyboard, or any "put these materials on a canvas" request.

Describe WHAT goes on the canvas; node ids, parent links and layout coordinates are generated for you. Items are laid out on a fixed-column grid (4 per row by default) and every image/video node keeps the real pixel size of its asset.

Text is NOT supported on the canvas: never pass type="text" entries. Titles, section names and captions belong in your chat reply, not on the canvas. Invalid entries (text entries, missing files, …) are SKIPPED — the remaining valid entries are still written, and the result lists what was skipped and why.

- action="create": write a new canvas (overwrites the file if it already exists). Omit `items` (or pass an empty array) to create a blank canvas with a single default page — use this when the user just wants "a new canvas" to fill in themselves.
- action="update": read the existing canvas, then add / replace items by `id` and remove those listed in `remove_item_ids`. Items you do not mention are kept as-is.

Images and videos are referenced by `source_path` (absolute local path). They are COPIED next to the canvas file into a `<name>_assets/` folder, so the canvas stays self-contained and portable.

IMPORTANT: this tool only writes the file — it does NOT make the canvas visible anywhere. After it succeeds you MUST do BOTH of the following with the returned `file_path`:
  1. `present_files` — include the `.miora` `file_path` in `files` (FIRST), then every path from the returned `copied_assets` so the images/videos also get their own artifact cards. Skipping this leaves the user with NOTHING in the artifact panel. Always deliver `copied_assets`, never the original `resultFiles[].localPath` from the generation tools: those live in a hidden plugin directory and never become artifacts.
  2. `miora_open_canvas` — open the canvas in the side panel for immediate viewing. This only opens a panel; it does NOT register any artifact card.

a9346d6867266d5f76eb21ad50e8baa8.name: miora_open_canvas
a9346d6867266d5f76eb21ad50e8baa8.description:
Open a `.miora` canvas file — call this after `miora_write_canvas` so the user can see the canvas immediately. The canvas is registered as an artifact card and opened automatically; it renders as an interactive read-only board.
You do NOT need to also call `present_files` for this canvas — doing so would just register the same file twice.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: batch_edit
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Execute multiple insert/copy/update/move/delete/image operations in a single call.

## Usage

- Keep each batch_edit call to **maximum 25 operations** for optimal performance.
- For larger designs, split work into multiple batch_edit calls by logical sections (e.g., screen structure first, then sidebar content, then main content).
- Avoid creating large operation objects like an insert with multiple descendants. Prefer breaking it down into many separate operations instead.
- If one of the operations fails, all previously executed operations in that block will be rolled back.
- Important: always create new binding names for every operation list, DO NOT reuse binding names across operation lists.
- A list of potential issues will be returned in the response message. Try to fix them in the next batch_edit call.

### Key Points

- Every Insert (I), Copy (C) operation MUST have a binding name. To reference a parent node in later operations, use the binding name from an earlier Insert, Copy operation in the same operation list.
- Not all bindings need to be used as parents later - it's okay to have "unused" bindings. The requirement exists to enforce deliberate structure.
- Bindings only work within the same batch_edit call for parent references
- Operations execute sequentially; on error, all operations in the list will be rolled back.

### Operation list format

You can create a list of operations in the following syntax:

- Every single operation must follow the Javascript syntax described below.
- ONLY these operation functions are supported.
- Every single operation line must be a single operation call with a possible binding assignment and nothing else.
- For node data, always follow the .ardot schema.
- This parent node will be used for the operations inserted/copied/moved. For these operations defining a parent is REQUIRED.
- The Page Node does not have a binding name, always use the page node's ID as the parent to Insert in page.

### Working with Existing Frames

- Use the frame's ID directly as the parent: `existingFrameId`
- If you update a frame's layout properties, insert children INTO that same frame using its ID

### Using bindings for paths and node ids

- You can use a binding variable name instead of an inline string an operation call
- If you want to combine it with some other binding or a string use the "+" operator
- IMPORTANT: DO NOT try to Update (U) a node's descendant that you just copied (C), since copying will recreate the descendant nodes and it will assign new IDs to those children nodes.

For example:

``` javascript
foo=I("pageId", { type: "ref", ref: "caSd2fv" })
U(foo+"Csawf3", {content: "+240%"})
D(foo)
```

Example - Adding content to existing frame "MmNEt":

``` javascript
U("MmNEt", {layout: "horizontal", gap: 16})
sidebar=I("MmNEt", {type: "ref", ref: "JRlf7", width: 240})
content=I("MmNEt", {type: "frame", layout: "vertical"})
header=C("A2sa3f", content, {width: "fill_container", height: "fill_container"})
```

### Response

A list of created or updated nodes and their updated properties.

### Insert (I)

Definition: insertedNodeId=I(parent: string, nodeData: Schema.Child)

- Important: "id"s are always created automatically for nodes, never create "id" properties in new node data.
- To insert an SVG node, use `type: "frame"` with a `svg` property containing the SVG string. The SVG will be parsed and converted into a FrameNode with vector children. You can set additional properties like `name`, `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` alongside `svg`.
- An insert can only be a single node, if you want to add children to it, use bindings and do it in a new Inert (I) operation.
- When working with components (reusable: true), insert their instances as refs with their properties overridden. If you want to override properties of subcomponents use subsequent Update (U) operations.
- Returns the inserted node ID as string
- **IMPORTANT:** Every created node must be actively assigned a meaningful `name`.
- **IMPORTANT:** Never insert nodes into an instance node or any instance node children, because they are virtual nodes and cannot be add new nodes.

### Copy (C)

Definition: copiedNodeId=C(path: string, parent: string, copyNodeData: Schema.Child & { positionPadding?: number; positionDirection?: string })

- When copying a node and modifying its descendants, you MUST use the "descendants" property in the Copy operation itself. DO NOT use separate Update operations for descendants of copied nodes, as this will fail due to ID mismatches. The copied node and its descendants receive new IDs, so Update operations referencing the original descendant IDs will fail.
- "path": The ID of the existing node to copy. If you want to customize some properties of the copied node, just add them next to the 'path' property. If you want to customize nested nodes _under_ the copied one, use the same kind of 'descendants' map that 'ref' nodes use!
- "descendants": Optional, used for components. An object which keys are node IDs or paths to descendant objects inside the component used to customize the properties of descendant objects.
- Example of correct usage: 'label1=C("NKYzH", container, {"descendants": {"ZopUS;jEYMs": { "content": "First Name" }}})'
- "positionPadding": The minimum padding distance from other element when positioning if needed.
- "positionDirection": The direction to search for empty space relative to the node, to position the copied node if needed. Possible values are: "top", "right", "bottom", "left"
- Copying a reusable node creates a connected instance (a 'ref' node).
- Returns the copied node ID as string

### Update (U)

Definition: U(path: string, updateData: Schema.Child)

- Update the properties of existing nodes, without listing their children.
- Use this operation to create small incremental updates to the properties of existing nodes.
- This operation CANNOT change the 'id', 'type' or 'ref' properties of any node!
- "path": The valid ID of the existing node to update (DO NOT use bindings in "path"), or if you want to update a nested node inside a instance, use the ID of the nested node must be prefixed with the ID of the instance and a (;). E.g. consider this component:
{
	"id": "button",
	"type": "frame",
	"reusable": true,
	"children": [{ "id": "container", "type": "frame", "children": [{"id": "label", "type": "text", "content": "Button text"}] }]
}
And then an instance of this component like this: {"id": "submit-button", "type": "ref", "ref": "button"}
The label text of 'submit-button' can be changed by passing the following as the "nodes" parameter:

``` javascript
U("submit-button;label", {content: "Submit"})
```

This slash-separated instance ID scheme works for any number of nesting levels, not just two.

- "updateData": The node data to update

### Move (M)

Definition: M(nodeId: string, parent: string | undefined, index?: number)

- Move a nodes to a different location in the node tree in a .ardot file.
- "path": The id of the moved node. ALWAYS use a valid node id, NOT a path or binding.
- "parent": Optional parent node Id or binding
- "index": Optional new position of the moved node among its siblings. If omitted, the node is placed at the end.

### Delete (D)

Definition: D(nodeId: string)

- Delete a node from a .ardot file.
- "nodeId": The ID of the node to delete. ALWAYS use a valid node id, NOT a path or binding.

### Placeholder Image (G)

Definition: G(nodeId: string, type: "placeholder", prompt: string)

- IMPORTANT: There is NO "image" node type! Images are applied as FILLS to frame/rectangle nodes.
- **`G()` is placeholder-only.** `"type"` must be `"placeholder"`. 
- Do not invent random URLs or `IMAGE` fills.
- To show a labeled gray box: first Insert a frame or rectangle, then `G` to apply the placeholder fill.
- "nodeId": The ID of the frame/rectangle node to apply the fill to. Can be a valid node ID or a binding name (e.g., "myFrame") created earlier in this operation list.
- "type": `"placeholder"` only — a gray box with the label from `prompt` centered on it. No real image asset, no image-generation budget. Use for drafts / wireframes, or when ImageGen is unavailable / undesired.
- "prompt": a **short label** (≤ 20 chars, ~2–4 words) shown on the placeholder, e.g. `"Hero image"`, `"User avatar"`. NOT a full AI prompt — long text overflows and looks broken. The label MUST be written in the same language as the user, e.g. Chinese labels like `"封面图"`, `"用户头像"` when the user speaks Chinese.

Example — placeholder (drafts/wireframes; SHORT label ≤ 20 chars):

``` javascript
avatar=I("parentId", {type: "frame", name: "Avatar", width: 120, height: 120})
G(avatar, "placeholder", "User avatar")
```

### Examples

**Example: Dashboard layout structure (8 ops)**

Add Sidebar and main content structure to a dashboard frame. Prefer adding components directly into an existing frame.

``` javascript
sidebar=I("29c0s", {type: "ref", ref: "JRlf7", x: 0, y: 0, width: 240, height: "fill_container"})
mainContent=I("29c0s", {type: "frame", layout: "vertical", gap: 24, padding: 32})
stats=I(mainContent, {type: "frame", layout: "vertical", gap: 16})
card1=I(stats, {type: "ref", ref: "QMBKc", width: "fill_container", height: "hug_contents"})
card2=I(stats, {type: "ref", ref: "QMBKc", width: "fill_container", height: "hug_contents"})
card3=I(stats, {type: "ref", ref: "QMBKc", width: "fill_container", height: "hug_contents"})
U("FVge3x;vdS2egl", {width: "fill_container", height: "fill_container"})
U("FVge3x;gDsgE6S", {content: "Submit"})
```

**Example: Form inputs section (8 ops)**

Add form inputs with labels to an existing content area.

``` javascript
label1=I("mainContent", {type: "ref", ref: "NKYzH"})
U(label1+"ZopUS;jEYMs", {content: "First Name"})
input1=I("mainContent", {type: "ref", ref: "FmgD2", width: "fill_container"})
U(input1+"CvD2R", {content: "First Name"})
input2=I("mainContent", {type: "ref", ref: "FmgD2", width: "fill_container"})
U(input2+"CvD2R", {content: "Last Name"})
U(contact+"oknii", {content: "Full Name"})
```

This example inserts a component directly into an existing frame.

``` javascript
sidebar=I("d3902", {type: "ref", ref: "JRlf7", x: 0, y: 0, width: 240, height: "fill_container"})
```

Copying a non-reusable frame (e.g., duplicating a screen). This copies the dashboard created above and tweaks it as another variation:

``` javascript
dashboardV2=C("Xk9f2", "pageId", {name: "Dashboard V2", positionDirection: "right", positionPadding: 100})
D(dashboardV2+"sidebarId")
U(dashboardV2+"statsId;card1Id", {fill: "#E8F5E9"})
U(dashboardV2+"statsId;card2Id", {fill: "#FFF3E0"})
```

**Important:** When creating icons, prefer SVG node over icon fonts.

**Important:** Inserting an SVG node. Use `type: "frame"` with a `svg` property containing the full SVG markup:

``` javascript
triangle=I("parentId", {type: "frame", svg: "<svg width=\"261\" height=\"109\" viewBox=\"0 0 261 109\" fill=\"none\" xmlns=\"http://www.w3.org/2000/svg\"><path d=\"M1 108L84 1L259 97L1 108Z\" stroke=\"black\"/></svg>", name: "Triangle Shape", x: 100, y: 50})
```

When setting fill colors, keep color values to 2 decimal places to avoid excessively long floating-point numbers.

``` javascript
U("nodeId", {fills: [{type: "SOLID", color: {r: 0.25, g: 0.48, b: 0.88}, opacity: 0.85, visible: true, blendMode: "NORMAL"}]})
```

Applying a gradient fill to an existing node. Use `fills` with `type: "GRADIENT_LINEAR"`, `gradientStops` (array of color stops), and `gradientTransform` (2x3 matrix), note that `gradientStops` array should have at least two elements, and `boundVariables` can be empty but must be present:

| gradientTransform Direction | Matrix |
|-----------------------------|--------|
| left → right | [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]] |
| right → left | [[-1, 0, 1], [0, -1, 1]] |
| top → bottom | [[0, 1, 0], [-1, 0, 1]] |
| bottom → top | [[0, -1, 1], [1, 0, 0]] |
| 45° (ur → ll) | [[1, 1, 0], [-1, 1, 0.5]] |

``` javascript
U("nodeId", {fills: [{type: "GRADIENT_LINEAR", gradientStops: [{color: {r: 0.2, g: 0.4, b: 1.0, a: 1}, position: 0, boundVariables: {}}, {color: {r: 0.8, g: 0.2, b: 0.8, a: 1}, position: 0.5, boundVariables: {}}, {color: {r: 1.0, g: 0.4, b: 0.3, a: 1}, position: 1, boundVariables: {}}], gradientTransform: [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0]], opacity: 1, visible: true, blendMode: "NORMAL"}]})
```

Supported gradient types: `GRADIENT_LINEAR`, `GRADIENT_RADIAL`, `GRADIENT_ANGULAR`, `GRADIENT_DIAMOND`.

**Example: Fixing layout alignment issues (3 ops)**

Fix a search bar where children are top-aligned instead of vertically centered, and distribute children to opposite ends (text on the left, button on the right). Use `counterAxisAlignItems: "CENTER"` for cross-axis centering, `primaryAxisAlignItems: "SPACE_BETWEEN"` for distributing children to both ends, and `layoutGrow: 1` to make a child fill the remaining space along the primary axis.

``` javascript
U("searchBar", {counterAxisAlignItems: "CENTER", primaryAxisAlignItems: "SPACE_BETWEEN"})
U("searchText", {layoutGrow: 1})
U("searchButton", {primaryAxisAlignItems: "CENTER", counterAxisAlignItems: "CENTER"})
```

**Example: Fixing text style inside a button (1 op)**

Fix button text color and size to ensure readability against the button background. Use `fills` to set text color and `fontSize` to adjust size.

``` javascript
U("buttonLabel", {fills: [{type: "SOLID", color: {r: 1, g: 1, b: 1}, opacity: 1, visible: true, blendMode: "NORMAL"}], fontSize: 14, fontName: {family: "Sarasa Gothic SC", style: "Bold"}})
```

## Common Property Mistakes — DO NOT USE These Invalid Properties

The following properties are **NOT supported** and will cause errors or be silently ignored. Always use the correct property name listed below.

| ❌ WRONG (Do NOT use) | ✅ CORRECT (Use this instead) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `textColor: "#FFF"` | `fill: "#FFFFFF"` | Text color is set via `fill` (a hex string), which maps to `fills` internally |
| `verticalAlign: "center"` | `counterAxisAlignItems: "CENTER"` | Use uppercase enum values for alignment |
| `alignItems: "center"` | `counterAxisAlignItems: "CENTER"` | `alignItems` is NOT a valid property |
| `justifyContent: "center"` | `primaryAxisAlignItems: "CENTER"` | `justifyContent` is NOT a valid property |
| `fontWeight: "bold"` | `fontWeight: "700"` | Use numeric strings: `"100"` to `"900"` |
| `fontWeight: "semibold"` | `fontWeight: "600"` | Maps to `"Semi Bold"` font style |
| `fontWeight: "medium"` | `fontWeight: "500"` | Maps to `"Medium"` font style |
| `fillColor: "#FFF"` | `fill: "#FFFFFF"` | Use `fill` for both text and shape colors |
| `backgroundColor: "#FFF"` | `fill: "#FFFFFF"` | Background color is just `fill` on a frame |
| `borderRadius: 8` | `cornerRadius: 8` | Use `cornerRadius` |
| `color: "#FFF"` | `fill: "#FFFFFF"` | Always use `fill` for colors |

### Font weight reference

Use **numeric strings** for `fontWeight`:

| Value | Font Style |
|---|---|
| `"100"` | Thin |
| `"200"` | Extra Light |
| `"300"` | Light |
| `"400"` | Regular |
| `"500"` | Medium |
| `"600"` | Semi Bold |
| `"700"` | Bold |
| `"800"` | Extra Bold |
| `"900"` | Black |

Default use `fontWeight: "400"`

### Font family reference

When creating a text node, you must specify the `fontName`, such as:

``` javascript
txt=I("nodeId", {type: "text", content: "...", fontSize: 16, fill: "#18191C", fontName: {family: "Inter", style: "Regular"}})
```

In general, you should use the font family and style that match your design system.
But if you want to use a specific font, you can specify it in the `fontName` property.
When not specified, use `Inter`.

**Important:** After creating text nodes, the system validates whether the fonts used are available. If a font is not available, you will see it in `potentialIssues`. To fix it:
1. Call `get_available_fonts` with the font family names to find their exact available styles
2. Pick an exact family + style match from the result
3. Use U() to update the text node's fontName with the correct font

Do NOT guess font style names — always use the exact strings from `get_available_fonts`.

### Alignment property reference

For frames with `layout: "horizontal"`, `layout: "vertical"` or `layout: "wrap"`:

> `primaryAxisAlignItems`, `counterAxisAlignItems` and `counterAxisAlignContent` will only work when the node has layout not `"NONE"`

| Purpose | Property | Valid Values |
|---|---|---|
| Main axis alignment | `primaryAxisAlignItems` | `"MIN"`, `"CENTER"`, `"MAX"`, `"SPACE_BETWEEN"`, `"SPACE_EVENLY"` |
| Cross axis alignment | `counterAxisAlignItems` | `"MIN"`, `"CENTER"`, `"MAX"`, `"BASELINE"` |
| Cross axis content (wrap) | `counterAxisAlignContent` | `"AUTO"`, `"SPACE_BETWEEN"` |

### Size property values

- **Numeric values**: `width: 400`, `height: 300` — sets exact pixel size
- **`"fill_container"`**: makes the node stretch to fill the parent's available space along that axis (requires parent to have layout)
- **`"fill_container(200)"`**: same as above, but with a minimum size of 200px
- **`"hug_contents"`**: makes the node shrink-wrap to fit its children

### Text color

Text nodes have **no visible color by default**. You MUST set the `fill` property:

``` javascript
title=I(parent, {type: "text", content: "Hello", fontSize: 16, fill: "#18191C"})
```

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: batch_read
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Retrieve nodes by searching for matching patterns and by node ids in batches.

- IMPORTANT: Combine multiple search patterns and node ID searches into one call.
- IMPORTANT: If you need to read some specific properties, specify them in the properties array.
- If neither patterns nor nodeIds is specified, returns the top-level children of the current page.
- Use searchDepth to define how many levels to search in.
- When a node with more than 500 children is read, the information of the child nodes will be compressed, retaining only the ID, name, type, and a compressed version of their children.
- When using design system components, AVOID reading each component one-by-one. Instead list all of the available components in a single tool call.

Traversing large documents:
1. Start by reading top-level nodes, or nodes you already know the IDs of to understand overall structure
2. Decide if the nodes you have already read are sufficient for your task
2. If you need more data and you see "..." for children, make new read calls with those specific child IDs

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: locate_available_space
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Find Available space in a .ardot file for a given direction and desired size.

- IMPORTANT: Always need call this tool before try to insert a node on root page.
If nodeId is provided, finds space around that specific node.
If nodeId is omitted, finds space around the entire canvas content.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: fetch_editor_state
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Get the currently active canvas editor, the current user selection and other essential design information to get started on a design task.

  - IMPORTANT: If you already loaded the 'ardot-design-assistant' skill, always set 'includeSchema' and 'includeGeneralEditInstructions' to false to avoid loading again.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: fetch_file_info
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Get basic information about the currently active design file.

- Returns the file name, file URL, file ID and the user's permission on the file.
- Use this tool when you need to know which file is currently being edited or to check whether the user has write access before performing edits.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: fetch_variables
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Get the variables defined in this design file, or the variable modes supported by a specified node.

- Use the result of this tool to create global CSS rules to use in a codebase.
- When generating code from a design, use this tool to get the global styling rules.
- To fetch a team variable library, pass `enabledLibraryKey` with that library's key, omit it to return only the current file's local variables.
- Team-library variable sets are returned with their `libraryKey`. Use the `$lib:<libraryKey>:<variableSetId>:<variableId>` syntax in `batch_edit` to bind the library variable.
- For large libraries, narrow the result with `type` / `scope` instead of fetching everything, to avoid flooding the context.

- IMPORTANT: To get the variable modes switchable on a node, pass `nodeId`. In that mode other parameters are ignored;

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: apply_variables
fetch_styles
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Fetch the full definition of local shared styles: FILL paints, TEXT font (fontFamily, fontSize, lineHeight, letterSpacing) and EFFECT paints.

Two modes:
- By id (preferred after search_styles): pass `styleIds` to load full detail only for the few styles you actually reuse. Up to 50 ids per call; unknown ids are skipped.
- List all: omit `styleIds` to enumerate every local shared style in the file, e.g. to build a style panel or audit the file's styles. Narrow with `styleTypes` to a single kind when you only care about colors, text or effects.

Only the current file's local styles are returned; use search_styles with `enabledLibraryKey` for team libraries.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: export_variables
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Export the design file's local variables as ready-to-consume code tokens.

# Output Formats
- `w3c-json`: W3C Design Tokens Community Group JSON. Nested groups from variable path; `$type` / `$value` / `$description`; multi-mode written to `$extensions.modes`.
- `css`: CSS custom properties (`--name: value;`). Multi-mode split by `:root` + `[data-theme="<mode>"]` blocks.
- `scss`: SCSS variables (`$name: value;`). Multi-mode produces one file per mode.

# Parameters
- `format`: `w3c-json` | `css` | `scss`. Required.
- `scope`: `'all'` (default) or an array of variable ids to include.
- `mode`: `'all'` (default) or a mode name to filter by. When `'all'`, `splitByMode` decides single-file vs per-mode files.
- `splitByMode`: when true and `mode = 'all'`, emit one file per mode (for zip packaging).
- `colorFormat`: `hex6` | `hex8` | `rgba` | `hsl`. Default `hex8`. `hex6` drops alpha; keep the default (or use `rgba` / `hsl`) to preserve transparency.
- `pathSeparator`: `-` (default) or `_`. Only affects CSS/SCSS variable naming.
- `numberUnit`: `px` (default) | `rem` | `none` for CSS/SCSS number values. Use `none` for unitless variables (opacity, line-height, z-index, font-weight).

# Behavior
- Aliases are preserved as references (`{path.to.var}` in JSON, `var(--...)` / `$name` in CSS/SCSS); cross-collection aliases include the collection name.
- Referenced-but-deleted variables inline the resolved terminal value with a `$extensions.warning`; absent targets yield `null` + a missing warning.
- Circular alias chains cause the export to fail with the list of variable paths involved.
- Response is `{ files: [{ name, content }], estimatedTokens }`. Write each file by `name`; use `estimatedTokens` (chars/4) to decide whether to re-call with a narrower `scope` when the payload is large.
- Output content is byte-identical to what the manual download in the design file's variable panel produces for the same options.
- Read-only: never mutates the file.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: capture_layout
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Check the current layout structure of an design file.

- Be careful with omitting the maxDepth parameter, as large maxDepth values can result in a lot of data.
- If you're only interested in layout problems like text lineHeight, overlapping elements, clipped elements, or large unused container regions, then use the problemsOnly parameter.
- maxDepth=1 means only the top level nodes layout in th parentId container will be returned.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: scan_exportable_resources
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Scan a node tree and return all exportable resource nodes, categorized by type.

- Accepts a root node ID and recursively scans its descendants.
- Returns a map with two lists: "image" (nodes with image fills, should be exported as PNG/JPEG/WEBP) and "svg" (nodes with only vector/shape elements, can be exported as SVG).
- Use this tool BEFORE export_nodes to determine which nodes to export and in what format.
- If nodeId is omitted, scans the current page.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: get_available_fonts
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Search available fonts by keywords. Returns matching font families with their available styles.

Response format: { fonts: [{ family: "Inter", styles: ["Regular", "Bold", "Semi Bold", ...] }, ...], totalFamilies: 5, truncated: false }

Usage:
- Use the `keywords` parameter to search for fonts by family name. Pass one or more terms in a single call (e.g. keywords: ["Inter"], keywords: ["Noto Sans", "Sarasa", "Roboto"]).
- If no keywords are provided, returns a default set of commonly used fonts.
- If the result is truncated, narrow your search with more specific keywords.
- You MUST use the exact family and style strings from this list in fontName properties.
- Example: if the response contains {family: "Inter", styles: ["Regular", "Semi Bold"]}, use exactly fontName: {family: "Inter", style: "Semi Bold"}.
- DO NOT guess or invent font style names — a mismatch like "semibold" vs "Semi Bold" will cause a missing font error.
- If your desired font is not in the list, try searching with different keywords.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: create_new_page
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Create a new empty page (CANVAS) in a .ardot file.

IMPORTANT: Do NOT call this tool casually. Only use it when the user explicitly asks to create a new page, or when starting a brand-new design task that must be isolated from the current page.
IMPORTANT: When generating multiple Slide pages, do NOT treat each Slide as a new page — do NOT call this tool for them. Lay out the slides within the same page instead.

- Adds a fresh blank page to the current document.
- If `leftPageId` is provided, the new page is inserted **immediately after** that page;
  otherwise it is appended next to the current active page (host default).
- If `name` is provided, the page is renamed to that value after creation.
- By default the editor switches focus to the newly created page (`select: true`).

Returns the newly created `pageId` (use it as `parentId` when later inserting top-level
frames via `batch_edit`).

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: search_style_guide
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Search the curated design catalog for candidates across 6 domains: style, color, typography, layout, scene, composition.

When to use: Visual design tasks needing creative direction (landing pages, dashboards, app screens, brand work). Call before `build_style_guide` whenever the user asks for a specific aesthetic, style, or mood, or when designing from scratch.

Input: `styleKeywords` is required; the other five `*Keywords` are optional. **All keywords MUST be English** — the catalog is English-only and non-ASCII input is rejected.

Output: Per-domain candidate lists, each entry `{ index, score, name, summary, bestFor }`. Pick by `summary` + `bestFor` against user intent — NOT by raw `score`.

Then call `build_style_guide` with the chosen `name` (or `index`) per domain to materialize concrete design tokens.

Call this ONCE per design task — do not re-search to retry or broaden. If no candidate fits a domain, pick the closest one and adjust on the build result instead.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: build_style_guide
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Materialize selected candidates from `search_style_guide` into a concrete design system JSON.

When to use: After picking candidates from `search_style_guide`. Always call this before drawing.

Input: For each domain (style / color / typography / layout / scene / composition) pass either the `index` (number) or the `name` (string) returned by `search_style_guide` as a top-level parameter. A domain may be omitted if no candidate fits.

Output: `{ design_system: { style: {...}, color: {...}, ... } }` with concrete tokens (hex, spacing, font family, shadow, radius). Field names match CSV columns (e.g., `background_primary`, `radius_card`). Read values directly via path access — do NOT scan text for tokens.

The returned design system is AUTHORITATIVE: use exact values as-is. If a domain conflicts with user intent (e.g., user wants dark, palette is light), do NOT re-search — adjust the minimum set of token values within that same domain (preserving structural relationships: Background/Foreground/Card contrast, Heading/Body font roles, radius hierarchy). Domains you explicitly omitted may use your own design knowledge freely.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: register_assets
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Request a temporary upload URL and a paired download URL for an asset.

- Use this tool to obtain a place to upload a local/generated asset binary before using it in other tools.
- Upload the asset to the returned uploadUrl (HTTP PUT), then pass the returned downloadUrl to any MCP tool that needs a resource URL.
- Example upload:
  `curl -X PUT '<uploadUrl>' -H 'Content-Type: image/png' --data-binary '@/path/to/image.png'`
  Replace `Content-Type` with the same MIME type you passed as `contentType` (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, or text/html).
- The URLs are temporary and may expire; request new ones if an upload fails after expiry.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: html_to_ardot
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Convert a remote HTML page into editable layers on the current Ardot design page.

- The HTML must already be uploaded to a temporary download URL (use register_assets first).
- Pass the download URL as htmlUrl.
- isSlide (boolean, default false): when true, import the root node as a Slide. For PPT / presentation scenarios, always set isSlide to true.
- Success: { success: true, fileId?, sessionId?, createdNodeIds?, batchEditOperations? }.
- If batchEditOperations is present, immediately call batch_edit with operations set to that string (prebuilt G image-gen ops). Split into chunks of ≤25 ops if needed.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: fetch_component_lib
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Get the components and component sets from a component library.

- When `libraryKey` is omitted or set to `'local'`, returns the **local** component library of the currently active file (i.e. components/component sets defined in this document).
- When `libraryKey` is a remote team library key, returns components published in that remote library.
- Use this tool to discover reusable components before creating instances via `batch_edit`.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: capture_screenshot
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
This tool returns screenshot images of one or more nodes in a design file.

This is a scarce visual-verification resource, not a routine check. Each call is expensive. Treat it as a last-resort audit after a completed batch of edits — never as a progress monitor.

HARD RULES:
- QUOTA: For one repair batch (all related edits for the current task or section), you may call this tool at most twice — typically once. The first call is allowed only after ALL planned fixes in the batch are applied. A second call is allowed only after you extracted EVERY issue from the first screenshot and applied those fixes together.
- NO INCREMENTAL LOOPS: Never screenshot → fix one small issue → screenshot again. Never screenshot after each batch_edit. Never screenshot to "see if it looks better" after a tiny tweak.
- PREFER capture_layout(problemsOnly: true) for spacing, overlap, clip, overflow, and hierarchy issues.

Usage:
- Pass ALL node IDs to verify in a single call via the 'nodeIds' array (less than 10). Never split one verification into repeated calls.
- After a screenshot returns, you MUST read and analyze every image before editing further. Extract ALL visible issues at once.
- Avoid nodes whose width or height exceeds 2000; screenshot each section instead.
- The saved screenshot location is returned for each node.

Each screenshot is uploaded automatically and a URL is returned in the result. Use curl or any other HTTP client to download the screenshot image.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: download_source_media
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
This tool downloads the original source media from a node's fill (not a rendered screenshot).

Usage:
- Pass a single node ID via 'nodeId'. The node must have a downloadable fill media. The topmost / last visible IMAGE fill with a non-null imageHash is used.
- Unlike capture_screenshot / export_nodes, this returns the source asset as stored (ignores crop / scaleMode / node size). Use it when you need the original fill media for editing, analysis, or re-upload.
- The saved file location is returned.

The source media is uploaded automatically and a URL is returned in the result.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: export_nodes
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Export nodes to image or document files in PNG/JPEG/WEBP/SVG/PDF/PPTX formats.

- Takes an array of node IDs and exports each one as a separate image file.
- For SVG format there is no limit on the number of nodes per call. For image formats (PNG/JPEG/WEBP), it is recommended to export no more than 5 nodes per batch.
- For PDF format, all Frame nodes in `nodeIds` are merged into a single PDF file (one file is written regardless of how many node IDs are provided). If no Frame node is included in `nodeIds`, falls back to exporting all frames on the current page. Frames are ordered top-to-bottom, then left-to-right (not by the order in `nodeIds`).
- For PPTX format, all Slide nodes in `nodeIds` are merged into a single presentation (one slide per node). If no Slide node is included in `nodeIds`, falls back to exporting all slides on the current page. Slides follow the layer panel order from top to bottom (not the order in `nodeIds`).
- Supports PNG, JPEG, WEBP, SVG, PDF and PPTX formats.
- File naming: each exported file uses an auto-generated name based on its node ID (a timestamp is appended to avoid overwrites).
- Returns a map keyed by node ID to the exported file's location. For PDF and PPTX, the map contains a single entry.

Each exported file is uploaded automatically and a URL is returned for each node.
- Uses 2x scale and high-quality settings by default.
- SVG export always uses 1x scale regardless of the scale parameter.
- PDF and PPTX export ignore the `scale` parameter.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: fetch_guidelines
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
This tool returns the design guidelines and rules for working with .ardot files.
Usage:
- IMPORTANT: Follow the guidelines and design rules to solve your design tasks.
- Call this tool multiple times with different topics to retrieve the relevant guidelines based on what you will work on next.
- This tool provides essential information about the ardot file schema, components, layout, positioning, typography, and other design rules.

Available topics:
- table: Guidelines to work with tables in Ardot. Use this when asked to insert, update or move tables or dashboards.
- landing-page: Guidelines for designing high-conversion landing page websites from scratch. Use this when asked to design landing pages, websites, or promotional web pages.
- web-app: Guidelines for designing web apps from scratch. Use this when asked to design web apps or web websites.
- mobile-app: Guidelines for designing mobile apps from scratch. Use this when asked to design mobile apps or mobile websites.
- slides: Guidelines for designing slides for presentations. Use this when asked to design slides for presentations.
- posters: Guidelines for designing posters. Use this when asked to design posters.
- code: Coding guidelines to generate code from Arodt design files. Use this tool when your task involves generating code or implementations from ardot design files.
- tailwind: Tailwind v4 specific implementation guidelines. Use when implementing designs with Tailwind CSS.

97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.name: upload_images
97dbbdf23c81f652ae1b2ccd5b6277a4.description:
Upload image assets and apply them as fills to specified nodes. Supports batch operations.

- IMPORTANT: Before calling this tool, you MUST call `register_assets` for each image to obtain a temporary `uploadUrl` and paired `downloadUrl`.

a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.name: resolve_local_excel
a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.description:
解析本地 Excel 文件的 file_id 与 sheet_list。
通过 get_pool_status 查询 editorsdk 编辑器池；若文件未打开则自动调用 open_file 打开。

  - 省略 local_path → 解析当前默认 session（file_id="_default"）。

返回：{ file_id, local_path?, sheet_list: [{sheet_id,sheet_name,sheet_rows,sheet_cols}] }

a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.name: get_cell_ranges
a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.description:
读取若干指定范围内单元格的值。传入 A1 格式的范围引用数组（如 ["A1:C10", "F2", "H5:H20"]，每个元素是单个范围或单元格，不要在一个字符串里写逗号或多段)。返回所有范围内非空单元格合并后的 values（按 A1 地址作 key）。多范围比多次调用更高效。
单次最多返回约 2000 个单元格（跨所有 ranges 合计），按输入顺序消耗预算；超出预算时从触发上限的 range 起按行边界截断或丢弃，并在响应中标记 truncated + 路由提示。若数据量超限，应通过 run_command 编写 JS 处理脚本在服务端完成处理，避免大量数据进入上下文。

a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.name: set_cell_range
a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.description: WRITE. 按 A1 地址映射设置单元格值、公式、样式和边框，可选批量调整列宽/行高。传入 sheetName 和 cells（key 为 A1 地址，value 为单元格数据），样式放在 cellStyles 嵌套对象里。不支持顶层 cellStyles/borderStyles；样式和边框必须写在 cells[addr].cellStyles / cells[addr].borderStyles。必须显式设置 allow_overwrite=true 才能写入（无论目标格是否为空、是否只改样式）。若样式写入范围疑似停在 read_table 的截断可见边界，会被 blocked；先补读完整表头/目标行确认业务边界。每格在 value（字面内容，含以 = 开头的纯文本）和 formula（=SUM(...) 等会求值的公式）中二选一。详细字段结构见 prompt §4.2.3，决策树/反模式见 §4.6。

a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.name: read_table
a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.description:
读取工作表中的表格数据。自动探测表格边界、方向和表头，支持多表格检测。返回结构化的表头与单元格显示值（grid）。这是所有操作的第一步——先了解数据再做修改。
单元格值以 grid（行主序二维数组）承载：grid[r][c] 对应单元格 (start_row+r, start_col+c)，空位为 null、每行尾部连续 null 已裁剪（缺失尾格视为空）。
不返回公式与数字格式——需要时改用 get_cell_ranges（include_formulas=true 取公式，include_number_formats=true 取格式）。
注意：grid 可能只包含部分数据。未截断时 start/end 表示已探测边界；截断时 start/end 只表示本次返回的可见边界。该范围内的单元格可能包含未返回的数据，写入前须先确认目标为空。单个表格最多约 200 个单元格，超出会按行截断并用 has_more / truncated 标记；若 has_more=true，grid 仅为 start_row..shown_end_row 的样本，其后至 end_row 的行内容未返回——不要对未展示行做任何假设，须按 has_more_warning 给出的范围续读后再下结论；若 truncated=true，响应会附带 visible_end_* / actual_end_* / truncation_warning，用于确认完整表头或目标区域。
表头按方向写到 header_rows / header_cols：
  - ROW    → header_rows = [banner 行..., 列标题行]，data_start_row 指向第一行数据；
  - COLUMN → header_cols = [banner 列..., 行标题列]，data_start_col 指向第一列数据；
  - MATRIX → header_rows = [列标签行]（行标签从 grid 每行首列读取）。
取列名 / 行名 = header_rows[len-1] / header_cols[len-1]。写入前避开 header 区域（行号 < data_start_row 或列号 < data_start_col）以免覆盖表头。
需要全量数据时应通过 run_command 在服务端处理，避免大量数据进入上下文。

a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.name: run_command
a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.description:
执行 Apps-Script 风格的 JavaScript 脚本完成表格操作。脚本在本插件内置的 JS 运行时中执行，
SpreadsheetApp / Sheet / Range / Utility 等 API 由运行时通过 MCP 原子工具（sheet_set_cell_value 等）映射到上游 sheet-editor。
适用场景：图表、透视表占位、插入/删除行列、合并、排序、筛选等结构性操作，以及大数据处理。
sheet.getRowHeight(row) / sheet.getColumnWidth(col) 返回值单位为像素(px)；请在向用户展示结果时使用'像素'或'px'作为单位
sheet.setRowHeight(row, px) / sheet.setColumnWidth(col, px) 入参单位也是像素(px)，有效范围 [10, 1000]。

a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.name: search_data
a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.description:
在表格中搜索指定文本，返回匹配的单元格位置。
搜索结果可配合 get_cell_ranges 进行详细分析。
支持大小写敏感、整单元格匹配、正则表达式、搜索公式等选项。
默认返回最多50条结果，超出可使用 offset 参数分页获取。

a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.name: calculate_single_formula
a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.description:
试算单个公式并返回计算结果，不会修改文档内容。
公式必须以 = 开头（如 =SUM(A1:A10)）。
必须指定子表（sheet_id 优先，或 sheet_name）；anchor 影响相对引用的计算基准。

a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.name: calculate_formulas
a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.description:
批量试算多个公式并返回每个公式的计算结果，不会修改文档。适合在大批量 setFormulas / set_cell_range 写入前先 dry-run 一个 anchor 样本，或一次性验证多个 pattern。每个 formula 必须以 = 开头。
单次最多 100 个公式，每条公式必须指定 sheet_id（推荐）或 sheet_name。实现：单次调用上游 sheet_calculate_formulas，所有公式在一次 roundtrip 内完成评估。

a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.name: fill_formula
a36d930c0e0784b7b4b9adab42c0604f.description:
WRITE. 把一条 R1C1 公式按相对引用平移填充矩形区域，类似 Excel/Sheets 的 fill-down。
示例：anchor=A2, rows=10, formula_r1c1="=R[-1]C+RC[1]" 会在 A2..A11 写入
  A2: =A1+B2, A3: =A2+B3, ..., A11: =A10+B11
公式必须以 = 开头。R1C1 语法：R[n]/Rn = 相对/绝对行，C[n]/Cn = 相对/绝对列，RC = 本格，省略 [] 等价 0 偏移。单次最多写入 5000 格。

results.description_en: Create a brand-new Excel/XLSX workbook. The trigger is the user's intent to PRODUCE a new spreadsheet (not to edit an existing one). Accepts three kinds of inputs: (1) text-only requirements, (2) PDF/DOCX/PPTX attachments as content references, and (3) source .xlsx/.xls/.csv/.tsv files used solely as content references — the skill reads their data and generates a brand-new workbook (never edits the source in place). Do NOT use when the user's intent is to edit / analyze / pivot / clean the source spreadsheet itself, when the requested output is not a spreadsheet, or when the local attachment is not one of the supported types. Guides the main agent to write an openpyxl script and validate formulas through recalculation.

results.name: tencent-docs-sheetagent
results.description: 编辑、查询、分析、清洗、透视、排序、筛选、格式化既有 Excel/xlsx/xls/csv 表格文件， 构造公式、生成图表、增删行列、合并单元格。 当用户上传、引用或指向一份**既有**表格文件、并对其做上述行为时使用。 当用户意图是从零产出一份新工作簿时改走 tencent-docs-sheet-generation。 提供比 openpyxl 更强大的表格处理能力。
results.description_en: Edit, query, analyze, clean, pivot, sort, filter, and format existing Excel/xlsx/xls/csv spreadsheet files; build formulas, generate charts, add/remove rows and columns, merge cells. Use when the user references an existing spreadsheet and asks to perform any of the above. Route brand-new-workbook creation to tencent-docs-sheet-generation instead.
